-- Euclid's GCD by repeated subtraction. Two guarded rules do the work;
-- with `≫` both may fire in one cycle (swap, then subtract the result).
-- io_done is high for one cycle when the result is ready.
xblue module mkGcd;
  input Bool reset;
  input Bool start;
  input Bit#(8) a;
  input Bit#(8) b;
  Reg#(Bit#(8)) x <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bit#(8)) y <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bool) busy <- mkReg(0);

  method Bool    io_ready  = !busy;
  method Bool    io_done   = busy && y == 0;
  method Bit#(8) io_result = x;

  rule load (start && !busy);
    x <= a;
    y <= b;
    busy <= True;
  endrule

  rule swap (busy && x < y && y != 0);
    x <= y;
    y <= x;
  endrule

  rule subtract (busy && x >= y && y != 0);
    x <= x - y;
  endrule

  rule finish (busy && y == 0);
    busy <= False;
  endrule

  rule clear (reset);
    busy <= False;
  endrule

  -- finish runs first, so io_done (read by `interfaces` at the start of the
  -- cycle) is seen for one cycle, and a new load may follow at once
  schedule finish ≫ load ≫ swap ≫ subtract ≫ clear;
endmodule

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- reasoning
open XBlue

structure St where
  x : BitVec 8
  y : BitVec 8
  busy : BitVec 1

/-- One clock cycle of the design itself. -/
def next (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) : St :=
  let r := (mkGcd.design.cycle (.cons reset (.cons start (.cons a (.cons b .nil))))
              (.cons s.x (.cons s.y (.cons s.busy .nil)))).regs
  ⟨r.get mkGcd.x, r.get mkGcd.y, r.get mkGcd.busy⟩

-- The five rules, each as a plain function on the registers.
def finish (s : St) : St :=
  let fires := s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.y = 0#8
  ⟨s.x, s.y, if fires then 0#1 else s.busy⟩
def load (start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) : St :=
  let fires := start = 1#1 ∧ s.busy = 0#1
  ⟨if fires then a else s.x, if fires then b else s.y, if fires then 1#1 else s.busy⟩
def swap (s : St) : St :=
  let fires := s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.x < s.y ∧ s.y ≠ 0#8
  ⟨if fires then s.y else s.x, if fires then s.x else s.y, s.busy⟩
def subtract (s : St) : St :=
  let fires := s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.y ≤ s.x ∧ s.y ≠ 0#8
  ⟨if fires then s.x - s.y else s.x, s.y, s.busy⟩
def clear (reset : BitVec 1) (s : St) : St :=
  ⟨s.x, s.y, if reset = 1#1 then 0#1 else s.busy⟩

/-- The cycle as a story, in schedule order: finish, load, swap, subtract, clear. -/
def spec (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) : St :=
  clear reset (subtract (swap (load start a b (finish s))))

theorem next_eq_spec (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) :
    next reset start a b s = spec reset start a b s := by
  obtain ⟨x, y, busy⟩ := s
  simp [next, spec, finish, load, swap, subtract, clear, mkGcd.design, Design.cycle, mkGcd.schedule,
    mkGcd.interfaces, mkGcd.rules.load, mkGcd.rules.swap, mkGcd.rules.subtract,
    mkGcd.rules.finish, mkGcd.rules.clear, mkGcd.signature, Sched.run, Action.step,
    Action.fires, writesIf, State.write, State.cur, State.read, HList.set, HList.get,
    Expr.eval, Expr.binVal, Expr.cmpVal, Common.putR, Common.putW, Common.memAt,
    mkGcd.x, mkGcd.y, mkGcd.busy, mkGcd.reset, mkGcd.start, mkGcd.a, mkGcd.b]
  bv_decide

/-- What each rule must preserve: the gcd of the two registers. -/
def g (s : St) : Nat := Nat.gcd s.x.toNat s.y.toNat

theorem swap_keeps_gcd (s : St) : g (swap s) = g s := by
  by_cases h : s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.x < s.y ∧ s.y ≠ 0#8
  · simp [swap, g, h, Nat.gcd_comm]
  · simp [swap, g, h]

theorem subtract_keeps_gcd (s : St) : g (subtract s) = g s := by
  by_cases h : s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.y ≤ s.x ∧ s.y ≠ 0#8
  · have hs : subtract s = ⟨s.x - s.y, s.y, s.busy⟩ := by simp [subtract, h]
    rw [g, hs, g]
    simp only [BitVec.toNat_sub_of_le h.2.1]
    exact Nat.gcd_sub_self_left (BitVec.le_def.mp h.2.1)
  · simp [subtract, g, h]

theorem clear_keeps_gcd (r : BitVec 1) (s : St) : g (clear r s) = g s := rfl

/-- Each rule keeps the gcd, so the cycle keeps the gcd of whatever `load` left. -/
theorem spec_gcd (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) :
    g (spec reset start a b s) = g (load start a b (finish s)) := by
  simp only [spec, clear_keeps_gcd, subtract_keeps_gcd, swap_keeps_gcd]

/-- A busy cycle that has not finished keeps the gcd. -/
theorem busy_cycle_keeps_gcd (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St)
    (hb : s.busy = 1#1) (hy : s.y ≠ 0#8) : g (next reset start a b s) = g s := by
  rw [next_eq_spec, spec_gcd]
  obtain ⟨x, y, busy⟩ := s
  simp only at hb hy
  simp [load, finish, hb, hy, g]

/-- A load starts a computation of exactly `gcd a b`. -/
theorem load_starts_gcd (reset : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) (hb : s.busy = 0#1) :
    g (next reset 1#1 a b s) = Nat.gcd a.toNat b.toNat := by
  rw [next_eq_spec, spec_gcd]
  obtain ⟨x, y, busy⟩ := s
  simp only at hb
  simp [load, finish, hb, g]

/-- When it is done (`y = 0`), `x` is that gcd. -/
theorem done_is_gcd (s : St) (hy : s.y = 0#8) : s.x.toNat = g s := by
  simp [g, hy]

/-- Idle: nothing happens. -/
theorem idle_holds (s : St) (hb : s.busy = 0#1) : next 0#1 0#1 0#8 0#8 s = s := by
  rw [next_eq_spec]
  obtain ⟨x, y, busy⟩ := s
  simp only at hb
  simp [spec, finish, load, swap, subtract, clear, hb]

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- reasoning
open XBlue

structure St where
  x : BitVec 8
  y : BitVec 8
  busy : BitVec 1

/-- One clock cycle of the design itself. -/
def next (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) : St :=
  let r := (mkGcd.design.cycle (.cons reset (.cons start (.cons a (.cons b .nil))))
              (.cons s.x (.cons s.y (.cons s.busy .nil)))).regs
  ⟨r.get mkGcd.x, r.get mkGcd.y, r.get mkGcd.busy⟩

-- The five rules, each as a plain function on the registers.
def finish (s : St) : St :=
  let fires := s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.y = 0#8
  ⟨s.x, s.y, if fires then 0#1 else s.busy⟩
def load (start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) : St :=
  let fires := start = 1#1 ∧ s.busy = 0#1
  ⟨if fires then a else s.x, if fires then b else s.y, if fires then 1#1 else s.busy⟩
def swap (s : St) : St :=
  let fires := s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.x < s.y ∧ s.y ≠ 0#8
  ⟨if fires then s.y else s.x, if fires then s.x else s.y, s.busy⟩
def subtract (s : St) : St :=
  let fires := s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.y ≤ s.x ∧ s.y ≠ 0#8
  ⟨if fires then s.x - s.y else s.x, s.y, s.busy⟩
def clear (reset : BitVec 1) (s : St) : St :=
  ⟨s.x, s.y, if reset = 1#1 then 0#1 else s.busy⟩

/-- The cycle as a story, in schedule order: finish, load, swap, subtract, clear. -/
def spec (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) : St :=
  clear reset (subtract (swap (load start a b (finish s))))

theorem next_eq_spec (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) :
    next reset start a b s = spec reset start a b s := by
  obtain ⟨x, y, busy⟩ := s
  simp [next, spec, finish, load, swap, subtract, clear, mkGcd.design, Design.cycle, mkGcd.schedule,
    mkGcd.interfaces, mkGcd.rules.load, mkGcd.rules.swap, mkGcd.rules.subtract,
    mkGcd.rules.finish, mkGcd.rules.clear, mkGcd.signature, Sched.run, Action.step,
    Action.fires, writesIf, State.write, State.cur, State.read, HList.set, HList.get,
    Expr.eval, Expr.binVal, Expr.cmpVal, Common.putR, Common.putW, Common.memAt,
    mkGcd.x, mkGcd.y, mkGcd.busy, mkGcd.reset, mkGcd.start, mkGcd.a, mkGcd.b]
  bv_decide

/-- What each rule must preserve: the gcd of the two registers. -/
def g (s : St) : Nat := Nat.gcd s.x.toNat s.y.toNat

theorem swap_keeps_gcd (s : St) : g (swap s) = g s := by
  by_cases h : s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.x < s.y ∧ s.y ≠ 0#8
  · simp [swap, g, h, Nat.gcd_comm]
  · simp [swap, g, h]

theorem subtract_keeps_gcd (s : St) : g (subtract s) = g s := by
  by_cases h : s.busy = 1#1 ∧ s.y ≤ s.x ∧ s.y ≠ 0#8
  · have hs : subtract s = ⟨s.x - s.y, s.y, s.busy⟩ := by simp [subtract, h]
    rw [g, hs, g]
    simp only [BitVec.toNat_sub_of_le h.2.1]
    exact Nat.gcd_sub_self_left (BitVec.le_def.mp h.2.1)
  · simp [subtract, g, h]

theorem clear_keeps_gcd (r : BitVec 1) (s : St) : g (clear r s) = g s := rfl

/-- Each rule keeps the gcd, so the cycle keeps the gcd of whatever `load` left. -/
theorem spec_gcd (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) :
    g (spec reset start a b s) = g (load start a b (finish s)) := by
  simp only [spec, clear_keeps_gcd, subtract_keeps_gcd, swap_keeps_gcd]

/-- A busy cycle that has not finished keeps the gcd. -/
theorem busy_cycle_keeps_gcd (reset start : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St)
    (hb : s.busy = 1#1) (hy : s.y ≠ 0#8) : g (next reset start a b s) = g s := by
  rw [next_eq_spec, spec_gcd]
  obtain ⟨x, y, busy⟩ := s
  simp only at hb hy
  simp [load, finish, hb, hy, g]

/-- A load starts a computation of exactly `gcd a b`. -/
theorem load_starts_gcd (reset : BitVec 1) (a b : BitVec 8) (s : St) (hb : s.busy = 0#1) :
    g (next reset 1#1 a b s) = Nat.gcd a.toNat b.toNat := by
  rw [next_eq_spec, spec_gcd]
  obtain ⟨x, y, busy⟩ := s
  simp only at hb
  simp [load, finish, hb, g]

/-- When it is done (`y = 0`), `x` is that gcd. -/
theorem done_is_gcd (s : St) (hy : s.y = 0#8) : s.x.toNat = g s := by
  simp [g, hy]

/-- Idle: nothing happens. -/
theorem idle_holds (s : St) (hb : s.busy = 0#1) : next 0#1 0#1 0#8 0#8 s = s := by
  rw [next_eq_spec]
  obtain ⟨x, y, busy⟩ := s
  simp only at hb
  simp [spec, finish, load, swap, subtract, clear, hb]
